findings.title: Observer rebuild loses every mounted row sentinel
findings.what: The effect depends on rowCount and rootMargin. On either change, cleanup disconnects the old observer and clears elementIndex, intersecting, and pending. The new effect can only observe pending elements, but refs for already-mounted sentinels need not fire again, so pending is empty and the new observer tracks nothing. Visibility then remains stale or stuck on the initial slab, defeating viewport-bounded rendering and potentially hiding rows after the count changes.
findings.fix: Retain a current element-to-index registry across observer rebuilds and have each new observer register every connected element; remove individual entries when ref callbacks receive null. Add a rerender regression test that changes rowCount or rootMargin and then fires the replacement observer.
findings.acceptance: A test mounts 200 rows, rerenders with a changed rowCount or rootMargin, verifies the replacement observer observes existing sentinels, fires an intersection near row 100, and confirms row 100 becomes visible while the visible count remains bounded.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the cleanup at lines 96-101 clears every source of elements before the dependent effect recreates the observer, while lines 90-95 only flush pre-effect pending refs. The dispatched tests cover mount, intersection, and unsupported fallback but no dependency-changing rerender.

findings.title: Savings headline reports an all-turn share as a share of trivial turns
findings.what: trivialShare is calculated as trivialTurns / totalTurns, but the headline says that value is the percentage "of trivial turns" routed to Haiku. With the dispatched fixture, the calculation is 40/100 = 40%, while the wording claims 40% of the trivial-turn population rather than 40% of all turns. This misstates the denominator of an evidence-bearing savings recommendation.
findings.fix: Change the headline to say "routing 40% of turns to Haiku" (or calculate the actual proportion of trivial turns routed if that is the intended claim), and name the variable for its denominator.
findings.acceptance: Using the existing 100-total/40-trivial fixture, a test asserts the rendered headline says "40% of turns" and does not say "40% of trivial turns"; add a non-round fixture to verify the displayed percentage derives from trivialTurns/totalTurns.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 54 and 58 use different denominators in calculation and prose. The directly related baseline summary aggregation confirms totalTurns and trivialTurns are distinct aggregate fields; that comparison file is support only and is not included in findings[].files.
